create a library in the current directory, or in DIR (created if missing): a
self-contained library (its own entries and files, no pool), or with --pool
PATH a shallow library, which takes its entries from the library PATH and
links to its files. It asks no questions: every setting has a default (from
the global configuration, or built in), the options below override them, and
later changes go through `papers config`.

positional arguments:
  DIR                   directory of the library (default: the current
                        directory); like DIR, the paths of --bibtex,
                        --filesdir and --pool are relative to the current
                        directory

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -v, --verbose         say what papers does, step by step
  --debug               debugging messages, and the traceback of errors
  --color {auto,always,never}
                        colours and hyperlinks in the output: auto (default)
                        when the output is a terminal and the NO_COLOR
                        environment variable is not set
  --porcelain           output for programs (as git's): the standard output
                        has only the entries that the command added, modified,
                        renamed or removed, or found already in the library,
                        one per line: "added KEY", "modified KEY", "renamed
                        OLD NEW", "removed KEY", "existing KEY"; every other
                        message goes to the standard error (except the listing
                        of papers list, which stays on the standard output)
  --bibtex BIBTEX       bibtex file (default: papers.bib, or the first .bib
                        file of the directory)
  --filesdir FILESDIR   files directory (default: files, or an existing pdfs/,
                        papers/... folder)
  --pool PATH           a shallow library that uses the library PATH as pool
                        (PATH must be a library without pool; a relative PATH
                        is stored relative to the library): `papers add` looks
                        in PATH first and adds the new entries and their files
                        to it, and the library links to the files of PATH.
                        Default: no pool, a self-contained library
  --shallow             same as --pool with the default library (`papers
                        config --global default`)
  --global              also register the library as the default library (used
                        outside of any library, and by --shallow); DIR is
                        required (`papers init . --global` for the current
                        directory)
  --paths {relative,absolute}
                        file links in the bibtex relative to the bibtex
                        directory, or absolute (default: relative)
  --editor EDITOR       command to open a text editor; it must wait until the
                        editor is closed, e.g. vim or "subl -w"

duplicate check:
  An added entry is the same paper as a library entry when they have the
  same DOI, arXiv id, ISBN (two books), or else the same authors and title.
  The library entry keeps its key; fields only in the added entry are added
  and the file links are merged. An entry that brings nothing new is not
  asked about.

  --on-duplicate {ask,keep,update,skip,error}
                        what to do when the added entry is in the library,
                        with conflicting values or fields to add: ask
                        (dialogue; the default in a terminal), keep (merge,
                        conflicts keep the library's value: the library
                        receives the entry), update (merge, conflicts take the
                        value of the added entry), skip (leave the library
                        entry untouched, do not add), error (stop before
                        saving; the default without a terminal)
  --no-check-duplicate  disable duplicate check (faster, create duplicates)
  --no-pool             do not look in the pool first (by default, a PDF, DOI
                        or bibtex entry that is the same paper as a pool entry
                        is taken from the pool, with its files, without
                        fetching)
  --pool PATH           look in the library PATH first, instead of the pool
                        (PATH must be a library without pool): a paper that
                        PATH has is taken from it, with its files (copied as
                        the files mode says; in a shallow library, into the
                        files directory of its pool), and later `papers pull
                        --pool PATH` brings its corrections. Nothing is added
                        to PATH. Not the same as `papers -C PATH add`, which
                        adds to the library PATH.
  -u, --update-key      regenerate the key of the entries new to the library
                        from the key template (see "bibtex key format"
                        options). A duplicate always keeps the key of the
                        library.

metadata:
  The fields given here replace those found in the PDF, fetched from the
  DOI, or read from the added bibtex (one entry only). They do not change an
  entry already in the library (same DOI): use `papers edit`.

  --doi DOI             provide DOI -- skip parsing PDF
  --key KEY             the key of the entry (instead of a key made from the
                        key template); alone, the entry of that key is taken
                        from the pool
  --type TYPE           entry type (article, book...)
  --title TITLE         the title
  --author AUTHOR       the authors, e.g. "Smith, John and Doe, Jane"
  -a NAME [NAME ...]    same as --author (the values after the name are files
                        to add, as the FILE arguments). In papers v2, -a
                        FILE... attached files: when every value of -a is an
                        existing file (or a URL), they are attached as with
                        --attach, with a warning (until v4)

  --year YEAR           the year

  --no-query-doi        do not attempt to parse and query doi

files:
  What happens to the added PDF, the files of an added bibtex, and the
  attached files, is the `files` setting of the library (found: move): move:
  place them in the files directory, under a name made from the name
  template, and remove the original; copy: place them there, and keep the
  original (a hard link when possible, otherwise a copy); link: leave them
  where they are, the entry links to them there. A file that belongs to
  another library (inside its files directory) is never moved: it is copied
  instead. In a library that is shallow, the file links are those of the
  pool entry: move and copy place the files in the files directory of the
  pool, link leaves them where they are and the pool entry links to them
  there too.

  --attach FILE [FILE ...]
                        attach these files to the entry (e.g. supplementary
                        material)
  --move                files mode move, whatever the setting
  -r, --rename          same as --move
  -c, --copy            files mode copy, whatever the setting
  --link                files mode link, whatever the setting

  -e, --edit            edit entry
  -o, --open            open files

  --bibtex BIBTEX       bibtex file (default: papers.bib, or the first .bib
                        file of the directory)
  --filesdir FILESDIR   files directory (default: files, or an existing pdfs/,
                        papers/... folder)
  --pool PATH           a shallow library that uses the library PATH as pool
                        (PATH must be a library without pool; a relative PATH
                        is stored relative to the library): `papers add` looks
                        in PATH first and adds the new entries and their files
                        to it, and the library links to the files of PATH.
                        Default: no pool, a self-contained library
  --shallow             same as --pool with the default library (`papers
                        config --global default`)
  --global              also register the library as the default library (used
                        outside of any library, and by --shallow); DIR is
                        required (`papers init . --global` for the current
                        directory)
  --paths {relative,absolute}
                        file links in the bibtex relative to the bibtex
                        directory, or absolute (default: relative)
  --editor EDITOR       command to open a text editor; it must wait until the
                        editor is closed, e.g. vim or "subl -w"

filename format:
  --name-template NAME_TEMPLATE
                        python template for renaming files (default:
                        {authorX}_{year}_{title})
  --name-author-num NAME_AUTHOR_NUM
                        number of authors in the filename (not for {authorX})
                        (default: 2)
  --name-author-sep NAME_AUTHOR_SEP
                        separator of the authors in the filename (default: _)
  --name-title-word-num NAME_TITLE_WORD_NUM
                        maximum number of title words in the filename
                        (default: 100)
  --name-title-word-size NAME_TITLE_WORD_SIZE
                        minimum length of a title word: shorter words are left
                        out of the filename (default: 1)
  --name-title-length NAME_TITLE_LENGTH
                        maximum length of the title in the filename (the last
                        words are dropped until it fits; a longer first word
                        is cut) (default: 100)
  --name-title-sep NAME_TITLE_SEP
                        separator of the title words in the filename (default:
                        -)
  --name-unknown-template NAME_UNKNOWN_TEMPLATE
                        template of the filename of an entry without author,
                        year or title (default: unknown_{doi_or_id})
  --name-unknown-strict, --no-name-unknown-strict
                        the unknown template applies when the author, the year
                        or the title is missing; with this option, only when
                        all three are missing (default: False)

bibtex key format:
  --key-template KEY_TEMPLATE
                        python template for generating keys (default:
                        {author}{year}). The template applies to entries
                        generated from a PDF or a DOI; entries added from a
                        bibtex file keep their original key unless
                        -u/--update-key is passed.
  --key-author-num KEY_AUTHOR_NUM
                        number of authors in the key (not for {authorX})
                        (default: 2)
  --key-author-sep KEY_AUTHOR_SEP
                        separator of the authors in the key (default: _)
  --key-title-word-num KEY_TITLE_WORD_NUM
                        maximum number of title words in the key (default:
                        100)
  --key-title-word-size KEY_TITLE_WORD_SIZE
                        minimum length of a title word: shorter words are left
                        out of the key (default: 1)
  --key-title-length KEY_TITLE_LENGTH
                        maximum length of the title in the key (the last words
                        are dropped until it fits; a longer first word is cut)
                        (default: 100)
  --key-title-sep KEY_TITLE_SEP
                        separator of the title words in the key (default: -)
  --key-unknown-template KEY_UNKNOWN_TEMPLATE
                        template of the key of an entry without author, year
                        or title (default: {doi_})
  --key-unknown-strict, --no-key-unknown-strict
                        the unknown template applies when the author, the year
                        or the title is missing; with this option, only when
                        all three are missing (default: False)
